name: Kunsthalle Bern
known: Directors include Harald Szeemann (1961 to 1969), Valérie Knoll (2015 to 2022) and iLiana Fokianaki (since April 2024) (Wikipedia).

name: Kunstmuseum Bern
known: Nina Zimmer, the director, took over the Kunstmuseum Bern in August 2016 and is also director of the Zentrum Paul Klee (Wikipedia).

name: Centre d'Art Contemporain Genève
known: Founded by Adelina von Fürstenberg.
Directors since then were Paolo Colombo (from 1989, for thirteen years), Katya García-Antón (2002 to 2012) and Andrea Bellini (from 2012).

name: Usine Kugler (Fédération des Artistes de Kugler)
Kunsthaus Baselland
known: Founded by the Kunstverein Baselland in 1944 and run under it;

name: CAN Centre d'art Neuchâtel
known: A new team and a new association took charge in 2008, and in 2018 the director post was removed in favour of collective management (CAN).
Run by the non-profit association of the same name: a six-person office, a committee of artists and art historians chaired by Kyung Roh Bannwart, and about one hundred ordinary members (CAN).

name: Fondation Beyeler
known: Beyeler Museum AG board: Edgar Fluri (chair), James Koch, Georg Krayer, Eric Lohrer, Christoph Megert and Christoph Stutz (Basel-Stadt government, 2023).
Sponsors: the sponsoring page names projects titled Globus Public Art Project, UBS Artist Talks and the Piet Mondrian Conservation Project.

name: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen
known: Leadership: Josef Felix Müller (first artistic director), Dorothea Strauss (curator, 1996 to 2001), Gianni Jetzer (2001 to 2006) and Giovanni Carmine (since 2007) (Wikipedia).
Legal form: Verein Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen, governed by a board chaired in 2024 by Maria Nänny.

name: Fotomuseum Winterthur
known: The museum runs the SITUATIONS programme on photography in the digital age, led by director Nadine Wietlisbach, and the annual Plat(t)form forum for emerging European photographers (Wikipedia).

The Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach-Stiftung funds curator fellowships in photography at partner museums including this one, about 60,000 euros per fellowship (Krupp-Stiftung press release, 27 March 2025).

name: Kunsthalle Zürich
known: Directors: Bernhard Mendes Bürgi (1990 to 2001), Beatrix Ruf (2001 to 2014), Daniel Baumann (2015 to 2024) and Fanny Hauser (since 2025).

Governance: the Verein board is chaired by Michael Ringier, with Mirjam Staub-Bisang (treasurer), Gerd Schepers (vice-president), Barbara Gerber (representative of the City of Zürich), Chantal Blatzheim, Anette Bollag-Rothschild, Jürg Haller, Maja Hoffmann, Florian Rajki, Mark A.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich
known: Ann Demeester has been director since 2022 (Wikipedia).
Its 2024 annual report carries full accounts with an audit report and a logo image of funding partners, but names only the board chair.

name: Migros Museum
known: Founded in 1996 on the initiative of Arina Kowner, head of culture and social affairs at the Migros cooperative federation, and collection head Rein Wolfs, who became founding director.
Named for Migros, the retail cooperative whose founder Gottlieb Duttweiler began buying art in the mid-1950s.
Since 1 December 2023 a five-person collective runs the museum instead of a single director (e-flux).
It follows the model set by Migros cooperative founder Gottlieb Duttweiler, which mandates 1% of cooperative wholesale turnover for culture and education.

name: Shedhalle (Rote Fabrik)
known: Ketty Ghnassia is listed as management and Laura Amann Marín and Jen Kratochvil as artistic directors.
